publication.notes: The formal ICML PDF lists 10 authors beginning Peter Humphreys and uses Toby Pohlen. The landing lists Peter C Humphreys and Tobias Pohlen. The retained arXiv snapshot lists 11 authors, including Alex Goldin. These are preserved as distinct version-specific author lists; the publication field uses only the formal PDF list. The publisher issue date comes from citation_publication_date; the conference date range is retained separately and does not replace it. Publisher issue date is 2022-06-28; the July 17–23 conference range is an event date, not a substitute publication day. Publisher-hosted proceedings record; distinct from the retained arXiv preprint snapshot.
publication.title: A Data-Driven Approach for Learning to Control Computers
publication.venue: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning

name: A data-driven approach for learning to control computers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines reinforcement learning with behavioral priors from human interactions to learn computer control through keyboard and mouse actions.

name: DroidBot-GPT: GPT-powered UI Automation for Android
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Transforms Android UI states and available actions into language prompts for an LLM to choose and execute task steps.

name: Responsible Task Automation: Empowering Large Language Models as Responsible Task Automators
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. UI task automation is stated in the abstract, but its platform and detailed evaluation protocol are not identified.
summary: Presents ResponsibleTA, a coordinator-executor framework that checks command feasibility and task completion while using local memory for privacy-related controls. The paper compares prompted and learned implementations and evaluates them on UI task automation.

name: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available for this review. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. This is an application-specific automation benchmark grounded in recorded Excel user actions. Its execution interface is OfficeScripts, so it is adjacent rather than a visual GUI navigation benchmark.
summary: Introduces InstructExcel, a benchmark for generating Excel OfficeScripts from natural-language requests, built using scripts recorded from user actions and a collection of existing spreadsheets.

name: Intelligent Virtual Assistants with LLM-based Process Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract names Alipay but does not establish Android or iOS specifically.
summary: Presents LLMPA, a mobile process-automation architecture that decomposes requests, identifies interface elements, predicts actions and checks errors. Demonstrations evaluate multistep operations in Alipay.

name: UFO: A UI-Focused Agent for Windows OS Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UFO uses two agents to inspect Windows application interfaces and their control metadata, then grounds and executes user requests within and across applications. The study evaluates this UI-focused architecture on nine Windows applications.

name: ScreenAgent: A Vision Language Model-driven Computer Control Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines a screenshot-and-action dataset with a planning, acting, and reflecting loop for computer control through mouse and keyboard actions.

name: Enhancing Mobile "How-to" Queries with Automated Search Results Verification and Reranking
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Executes instructions from mobile how-to search results inside a controlled Android environment, then uses the observed success of those instructions to verify and rerank technical-support results.

name: Large Language Models for Mobile GUI Text Input Generation: An Empirical Study
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies language-model generation of mobile text inputs, comparing UI representations, execution feedback, and human assistance for app testing.

name: MMAC-Copilot: Multi-modal Agent Collaboration Operating Copilot
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces MMAC-Copilot, which coordinates agents with different expertise to operate PC applications. VIBench evaluates visual interaction with applications that lack usable APIs, spanning office, recreation and game tasks.

name: SmartFlow: Robotic Process Automation using LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents SmartFlow, which converts visible GUI elements into text for language-model action planning and executes the plan through a scripting engine. A collection of enterprise applications evaluates adaptation to different layouts and tasks.

name: Practical, Automated Scenario-based Mobile App Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ScenTest builds scenario-specific event knowledge graphs from crowdsourced test reports containing GUI and action information. It uses the current app state and testing context to generate scenario tests across applications.

name: Seeing is Believing: Vision-driven Non-crash Functional Bug Detection for Mobile Apps
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trident combines exploration, monitoring, and detection agents to identify functional bugs that do not crash a mobile app. It reasons over screenshot sequences and interface transitions to construct test oracles, evaluated on 590 non-crash bugs and additional live apps.

name: AUITestAgent: Automatic Requirements Oriented GUI Function Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Automates mobile GUI tests from natural-language requirements, combining action generation with verification based on interaction traces.

name: IDA: Breaking Barriers in No-code UI Automation Through Large Language Models and Human-Centric Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: IDA helps business users create web UI automation through guided demonstrations, a semantic programming model, and a teaching-oriented interface. A prototype user study examines automation creation with enterprise applications by users without programming backgrounds.

name: PeriGuru: A Peripheral Robotic Mobile App Operation Assistant based on GUI Image Understanding and Prompting with LLM
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: PeriGuru interprets smartphone GUI screenshots with computer vision and uses a language model to decide the next action. A peripheral robotic arm executes the phone interactions, providing an alternative mechanism for operating mobile apps.

name: NaviQAte: Functionality-Guided Web Application Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Frames web-application exploration as functionality-oriented question answering, generating navigation actions from multimodal context.

name: Steward: Natural Language Web Automation
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Steward, a natural-language browser automation system that repeatedly plans and executes website actions. The paper examines completion detection, state representation, responsiveness, and caching in real-site tasks.

name: AXIS: Efficient Human-Agent-Computer Interaction with API-First LLM-Based Agents
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AXIS, an API-first application agent that can use UI actions and expand its available APIs through automated application exploration. The work evaluates the approach on Microsoft Word tasks.

name: AgentStore: Scalable Integration of Heterogeneous Agents As Specialized Generalist Computer Assistant
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a platform that integrates specialized agents under a coordinating MetaAgent for varied computer tasks.

name: AutoGLM: Autonomous Foundation Agents for GUIs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents AutoGLM agents for browser and phone control, separating planning from grounding and training through an evolving interaction curriculum.

name: The Dawn of GUI Agent: A Preliminary Case Study with Claude 3.5 Computer Use
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents a preliminary study of Claude 3.5 Computer Use across desktop tasks and software, analyzing planning, action, and critique behavior and providing a framework for deploying GUI-automation models.

name: Large Action Models: From Inception to Implementation
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available for this review. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Uses a Windows-agent case study to describe a development workflow for large action models, covering data collection, training, grounding, environment integration, and evaluation.

name: GUI Testing Arena: A Unified Benchmark for Advancing Autonomous GUI Testing Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Evaluates GUI testing through test-intent generation, execution, and defect detection using real, modified, and synthetic mobile application data.

name: Programming with Pixels: Can Computer-Use Agents do Software Engineering?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a visual IDE environment and benchmark for software-engineering tasks, comparing screenshot-based control with access to editing and shell tools.

name: Towards Enterprise-Ready Computer Using Generalist Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes the CUGA enterprise-agent development process, emphasizing iterative evaluation, failure analysis, and refinement on software-task benchmarks.

name: API Agents vs. GUI Agents: Divergence and Convergence
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Compares API-driven and GUI-driven agents across architecture, development, and interaction considerations, discussing when hybrid approaches are useful.

name: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Adapts web agents to execute natural-language test steps, verify assertions, and issue test verdicts. The study introduces 113 passing and failing test cases across three offline web applications and compares two agent implementations with qualitative failure analysis.

name: ReuseDroid: A VLM-empowered Android UI Test Migrator Boosted by Active Feedback
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced. The platform or GUI evaluation setting was additionally checked in the primary full text.
summary: ReuseDroid migrates Android GUI tests between functionally similar apps using VLM agents that separate shared test intent from app-specific interaction flows. It introduces LinPro, a dataset of 578 migration tasks across 39 apps, to evaluate test transfer.

name: VLM-Fuzz: Vision Language Model Assisted Recursive Depth-first Search Exploration for Effective UI Testing of Android Apps
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: VLM-Fuzz combines depth-first UI exploration with Android manifest analysis, runtime widget hierarchies, and on-demand visual reasoning to generate app test inputs. It evaluates coverage on 59 benchmark apps and uses additional Google Play apps to study crash discovery.

name: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces UFO2, a Windows desktop agent architecture combining a coordinating HostAgent, application-specialized agents, and a shared GUI/API action layer. It integrates UI Automation, visual parsing, speculative planning, and an isolated picture-in-picture desktop.

name: LiteCUA: Computer as MCP Server for Computer-Use Agent on AIOS
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AIOS 1.0 exposes computer states and actions through an MCP server to provide structured environmental context for agents. LiteCUA is a lightweight agent built on this interface, evaluated on OSWorld to study the effect of computer-environment contextualization.

name: OS-MAP: How Far Can Computer-Using Agents Go in Breadth and Depth?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OS-MAP organizes 416 computer-use tasks across 15 applications by a five-level automation taxonomy and a hierarchy of user demands. The benchmark separates required autonomy from generalization scope to diagnose where agents struggle as task demands increase.

name: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-Agent System with Coding Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.

name: You Don't Know Until You Click:Automated GUI Testing for Production-Ready Software Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: RealDevWorld evaluates generated software repositories with 194 development tasks and AppEvalPilot, an agent judge that operates the resulting GUIs. The evaluation examines functional behavior, visual fidelity, and runtime responses to produce task-specific diagnostic feedback.

name: ScaleCUA: Scaling Open-Source Computer Use Agents with Cross-Platform Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a cross-platform computer-use dataset and agents trained with a collection pipeline combining automated interaction and human input.

name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

name: From Imperative to Declarative: Towards LLM-friendly OS Interfaces for Boosted Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a Declarative Model Interface that maps existing GUIs to access, state and observation primitives while handling low-level interactions. Evaluation uses Word, PowerPoint and Excel on Windows with a GUI-agent baseline.

name: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The short abstract supplies the framework and threat setting but no quantitative evaluation details.
summary: Proposes an in-browser fuzzing framework that uses language-model guidance to test indirect prompt-injection vulnerabilities in agentic browsers. The work focuses on unwanted actions triggered by webpage instructions under the browser agent's user privileges.

name: GAIR: GUI Automation via Information-Joint Reasoning and Group Reflection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GAIR, which combines information from specialized GUI models through a general-purpose coordinating model. When the available information is insufficient, group reflection sends targeted requests back to the specialists before selecting an operation.

name: GUITester: Enabling GUI Agents for Exploratory Defect Discovery
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GUITestBench for interactive defect discovery and GUITester, which separates task navigation from anomaly verification. Testing-oriented plans and history-based reflection help distinguish software defects from agent execution mistakes.

name: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CUA-Skill encodes Windows application knowledge in parameterized skills and execution/composition graphs. Its agent retrieves and instantiates these skills and uses memory for failure recovery, with end-to-end evaluation on WindowsAgentArena.

name: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.

name: See, Plan, Snap: Evaluating Multimodal GUI Agents in Scratch
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ScratchWorld evaluates program construction through the Scratch interface using fine-grained drag-and-drop actions and a complementary semantic-API mode. Runtime tests assess the resulting programs, allowing analysis of the gap between program reasoning and GUI manipulation.

name: WebTestPilot: Agentic End-to-End Web Testing against Natural Language Specification by Inferring Oracles with Symbolized GUI Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebTestPilot turns natural-language requirements into web test steps with inferred preconditions and postconditions over symbolized GUI elements. A benchmark of bug-injected web applications tests whether these context-aware oracles distinguish application defects from agent mistakes.

name: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Any Customized UI
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EmbeWebAgent embeds agent access into existing web applications through frontend observations and a page-specific function registry. Its workflow combines GUI primitives, composite actions and MCP tools, demonstrated in a live interface.

name: SpecOps: A Fully Automated AI Agent Testing Framework in Real-World GUI Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SpecOps divides testing of GUI-based agents into test generation, environment setup, execution and validation handled by specialist agents. Its evaluation spans five real-world agents, including web applications and browser extensions, and measures execution reliability and bug discovery.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.

name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.

name: Avenir-UX: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Avenir-UX combines grounded web interaction with simulated user profiles and structured usability measures to produce evaluations of website journeys. The paper describes its architecture and use of SUS, step-wise ease questions and think-aloud traces for automated UX reporting.

name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.

name: Training Computer Use Agents to Assess the Usability of Graphical User Interfaces
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: uxCUA learns to assess interface usability by choosing interaction flows, executing them and predicting a numerical usability score. Training uses interactive UIs with usability labels and human preferences, with evaluations on synthetic and real interfaces.

name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent computer-automation benchmark using terminal workflows, explicitly separated from graphical-interface control.
summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.

name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent GUI-application generation benchmark with real component interaction probes; its main evaluated agents are application coders, not general GUI task executors.
summary: VISTA evaluates coding agents that turn design handoffs into working web and Android applications. Its evaluator locates annotated interactive components and probes their behavior, keeping visual localization distinct from functional correctness.

name: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Adjacent computer-interface architecture: the described application command harnesses concern computer operation, but no GUI execution or comparative benchmark result is established in the abstract.
summary: CLI-Anything argues for application interfaces built around structured commands, explicit state and execution feedback. It describes transforming existing software into command-line harnesses and organizing that approach through CLI-Hub.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This study compares general coding agents using mobile command-line access with reproducible GUI agents on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld. It also supplies oracle CLI analyses and a separate task suite for operations such as bulk changes, filtering and hidden device state.

name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent general computer-operation benchmark: the evaluated interface is a terminal; GUI benchmarks are a contrast, not its execution modality.
summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.

name: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes a GUI foundation agent trained through expanded environments, function-grounded tasks, and trajectory verification with safety-aware execution mechanisms.

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: PhoneCLI: From App Interfaces to Callable Commands for Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.

name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.

name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.

name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.

name: Interaction-as-a-Judge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Uses computer-use agents to interact with generated applications, studying whether interaction improves preference judging, requirement checks, and feedback for application generation.
